messages:
Jonas T.: hi team 👋 joined product-platform today. Two quick setup puzzles: 1) VPN + kubectl access to dev clusters (I filled the SSO join but not able to kubectl) 2) Need to find the canonical owner for the 'payment-bridge' microservice so I can ask a quick question. Who should I ping and are there any shortcut approvals for kubectl during onboarding?

Marco - DevEx: welcome Jonas! for kubectl you need cluster-roles + namespace binding. Open the Access Portal and request 'dev-cluster-kube' with your GitHub handle and desired namespaces. If you include your use-case note (onboarding: run integration tests) we can auto-approve a read-only binding for 48h. Link: https://intranet.redwood/devex/onboarding.

Jonas T.: I added the request and put 'integration test run' in the justification. got "403 Forbidden" when trying `kubectl get pods -n redwood-dev` earlier.

onboard-helper-bot: Ticket ONB-4480 created for dev-cluster-kube by Jonas T. Status: pending.

Priya (Security): @Marco thanks for the tip. @Jonas for VPN ensure your SSO device is enrolled in our MDM. If your device isn't enrolled some access tokens are blocked. You can check enrollment at https://mdm.redwood/status (use corporate SSO). If MDM is missing, file a device onboarding request and tag security for expedited review.

Rita (Eng): for service owners we keep a simple ownership file in the repo and a cross-reference in Product docs. Quick find: repo: https://git.redwood/payment-bridge -> OWNERS.md shows primary: @alex (Payments), secondary: @tess (Platform). If you want I can ping them. Usually product-platform@redwood.com is a good alias for cross-team asks.

Jonas T.: thanks. can someone ping Alex? I need a 5-min question about an internal header the service expects.

Rita (Eng): pinged Alex and Tess in DM. Alex replied: "happy to help — ping me in 10m in #payments or DM for quick context."

Marco - DevEx: ONB-4480 should clear once MDM check passes and the Access Portal ties your SSO to the cluster-binding. Typical approval 20-45m during weekdays. If you need faster, reply here and we'll mark it high-priority. Also, pro tip: include `--requester-ssh-pubkey` in the access form so we can pre-add your key to bastion.

Jonas T.: I enrolled device in MDM and updated the access request with my pubkey and ticket ONB-4480. Quick Q: who do I page after-hours if a customer-facing integration test is failing because of access?

Priya (Security): after hours page sec-ops for security-related blocks, infra-oncall for cluster/network issues, and the payments oncall for service bugs. For onboarding-blocking access we treat it as P1 during business hours; after hours oncall triages and can escalate to an eng oncall.

onboard-helper-bot: ONB-4480 updated: dev-cluster-kube request approved. Binding: read-only (48h).

Jonas T.: confirmed kubectl read-only access works now. Also chatted with Alex — got the header detail. thanks everyone :raised_hands:

Marco - DevEx: adding a note to the onboarding checklist: include MDM and pubkey earlier in the flow to avoid wait time.

Priya (Security): also adding the escalation aliases to the checklist: infra-oncall, sec-ops, payments-oncall.

Jonas T.: perfect. feel free to @me if you want a quick note about where the messaging was unclear for new hires. really appreciate the quick responses!
